question: Can trajectory-grouped holdout evaluation with richer state representation (DOM tree structure with element roles) and semantic action selectors reveal genuine action-conditioned transition structure on live Web pages with navigational density, replacing the coarse URL+hash representation that produced entropy inversion in EXP-PHYSICS-33528829431?
hypothesis: When live Web transitions are collected from navigational-density sites using DOM-tree state representation and semantic CSS-selector actions, and evaluated with trajectory-grouped holdout (entire trajectories assigned to train or test, never split), the action-conditioned predictor accuracy on held-out trajectories will exceed the trajectory-grouped permutation null distribution at alpha=0.05 after Bonferroni correction across test sites. Specifically: (1) H(S'|S,A) < H(S'|S) on held-out trajectories, indicating action provides information about next state beyond current state alone; (2) the action-conditioned predictor significantly outperforms the permutation null (z > 1.96, p < 0.05 corrected); (3) the entropy reduction percentage is >5% on at least 2 of 3 test sites.
falsifier: The hypothesis is FALSIFIED if ANY of: (1) action-conditioned predictor accuracy on held-out trajectories is not significantly above the permutation null distribution (Bonferroni-corrected p > 0.05 across all test sites); (2) H(S'|S,A) >= H(S'|S) on held-out trajectories for all test sites (entropy inversion persists with richer representation); (3) the positive control fails (synthetic deterministic graph action-conditioned accuracy < 90% on held-out trajectories); (4) the null control fails (null control entropy reduction > 15%); (5) fewer than 200 valid transitions are collected across all test sites combined.
baselines: B_PERM_NULL: Trajectory-grouped permutation null — within each test trajectory, action labels are randomly permuted while preserving trajectory structure. The action-conditioned predictor is fit on permuted train data and evaluated on permuted test data. Repeated n_perm=1000 times to build a null distribution of accuracy values. This is the primary null model.

B_STATE_ONLY: State-only Markov predictor — predicts next state from current state only, ignoring action. Fit on trajectory-grouped train, evaluate on trajectory-grouped test. Tests whether action provides information beyond state alone.

B_ACTION_FREQ: Action-frequency predictor — for each action type, predicts the most common next state regardless of current state. Tests whether action identity alone (without state conditioning) carries predictive information.
B_SHUFFLE_ACCURACY: Shuffle baseline — same as B_PERM_NULL but reported as a single accuracy value (mean of permutation null distribution). Provides a point-estimate comparison.

B_PRIOR_COARSE: Replication baseline — using the coarse URL+hash representation from EXP-PHYSICS-33528829431 with trajectory-grouped holdout. Tests whether the representation upgrade changes observed dynamics.
positive_control: Synthetic deterministic navigation graph (5 states, 3 action types, 9 deterministic transitions) from EXP-PHYSICS-33528829431 substrate. Action-conditioned predictor must achieve >90% accuracy on HELD-OUT trajectories (trajectory-grouped split, not in-sample). This verifies the measurement pipeline correctly captures deterministic transitions when they exist, using the new evaluation method. The positive control uses overlapping actions across states (click appears in states A, B, C, D, E) to discriminate (S,A) from A alone.
null_control: Null control: synthetic random-click transitions where next state is independent of action (20 page states, 3 action types, 5 target IDs, random next state). Entropy reduction (H(S'|S) - H(S'|S,A)) / H(S'|S) must be < 15% on held-out trajectories. This verifies the pipeline does not detect action-conditioned structure when it is absent by construction.
measurement_validity: Trajectory-grouped holdout: entire trajectories assigned to train or test set. No transition from a test trajectory appears in train. This prevents information leakage between trajectories.

Trajectory-grouped permutation null: action labels permuted within each trajectory, preserving trajectory structure. Independent RNG per permutation with frozen seed sequence. Resamples trajectories, not transitions.

State representation: URL + DOM tree structure hash (hash of element tag hierarchy, attributes, and text content structure) + interactive element role hash (hash of element roles: button, link, input, select, etc.). Replaces coarse URL+structure_hash+element_hash.

Action representation: semantic CSS selector or ARIA role selector identifying the interactive element. Replaces link_N index-based actions. Actions must be identifiable by their semantic meaning, not positional order.
Positive control uses overlapping actions across states: 'click' action type appears in multiple states with different targets, enabling discrimination of (S,A) from A alone.
No target leakage: predictor features (state representation, action representation) never contain next_state information. Verified by structural check.
Seeds are deterministic: numpy RandomState with frozen seeds (42 for positive control, 43 for live test, 44 for null control). No Python hash() used as seed source.
Test sites have navigational density: at least 10 internal links per page average, enabling trajectory completion to 10 steps.
Minimum sample: >=200 valid transitions across all test sites combined for statistical power.

HTTP fetch + HTMLParser is the collection substrate (Playwright not available in current environment). This is a documented limitation — DOM tree structure is extracted from raw HTML, not from rendered/accessibility tree. Results survive another legitimate representation only if HTTP-fetched HTML preserves the relevant structural information.
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST if ALL of: (1) action-conditioned predictor accuracy on held-out trajectories exceeds permutation null at Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.05 across at least 1 test site; (2) positive control accuracy > 90% on held-out trajectories; (3) null control entropy reduction < 15%; (4) >=200 valid transitions collected; (5) no validity gate failures. FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING if: (1) action-conditioned predictor does not exceed permutation null at any test site after correction, OR (2) entropy inversion persists (H(S'|S,A) >= H(S'|S) for all sites), OR (3) positive control fails, OR (4) null control fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if: (1) <200 transitions collected, OR (2) validity gates fail, OR (3) infrastructure prevents execution.
product_consequence_positive: Demonstrates that richer state representation and proper evaluation reveal action-conditioned structure in live Web transitions. C-WEB-DYNAMICS advances from HYPOTHESIS. Product lane can investigate action-conditioned prediction mechanisms for exploration guidance. The measurement substrate (C-MEAS-VALID) is validated for live Web transition collection.
product_consequence_negative: If action-conditioned structure is not revealed even with richer representation and proper evaluation, C-WEB-DYNAMICS is weakened further. The claim that interactive Web transformations contain predictive dynamical structure beyond memory and ordinary similarity becomes harder to sustain. Physics lane should consider whether the claim is false or whether even richer representations (accessibility tree, rendered DOM, network responses) are needed. C-MEAS-VALID substrate may still be validated even if C-WEB-DYNAMICS is falsified in this setting.
estimated_cost: Low-moderate: HTTP fetches to 3 test sites (Wikipedia, BBC News, example.com), ~30 trajectories x 10 steps = 300 transitions. No browser automation, no model calls. Python stdlib + numpy (to be installed). Execution time < 5 minutes for collection, < 2 minutes for analysis. Total: ~1000 HTTP requests.
expected_information_gain: High: This is the first measurement-valid test of action-conditioned structure on live Web with (1) trajectory-grouped holdout preventing memorization, (2) trajectory-grouped permutation null with proper independence, (3) richer state representation, and (4) semantic actions. The prior experiment (EXP-PHYSICS-33528829431) was invalidated by in-sample evaluation, invalid bootstrap, and coarse representation. This experiment addresses all four defects. A positive result justifies advancing C-WEB-DYNAMICS; a negative result with this substrate constrains the claim and redirects Physics lane effort. Both outcomes are decision-relevant.
